findings.title: Delivery acknowledgement does not establish that an earlier result is no longer needed

candidate_anchors.relevance: Promises complete delivery of every result needed for the next decision, or refusal before the call.
Advances deliveredThroughStep after an accepted model decision; permits complete removal from selection and retention of already delivered observations.
Only results not yet delivered are mandatory.
Admission can remove optional items and proceed without them.

current_source_anchors.relevance: ModelGateway.complete is a request/response port with no durable model continuation or conversation-memory guarantee.
Current descriptive state is not a lossless archive of all previous tool outputs. This is context for the proposed change, not a claim that CURRENT already implements the proposal.

findings.concrete_counterexample: The goal requires returning the opaque strings from tools A and B together. Step 1 produces A. The next admitted, valid model decision receives A and requests independent B; persisting that decision advances the cursor through A. B then succeeds. At the following decision B is mandatory but A is optional and may even have been deleted. Choose A and B as independent 17000-byte ASCII strings: each is within the output limit and fits individually, while the combined user JSON exceeds 32000 UTF-16 units. The specified trimming may remove A and admit a request containing B only. A is still necessary to answer the goal, is absent from all other fields, and a stateless qualified synthetic model has no causal access to it. The proposal neither preserves that dependency nor requires refusal. Prior delivery alone cannot satisfy the invariant for this later request.
findings.material_impact: The proposal allows admission after loss of still-required complete evidence. This is a contradiction between its universal necessary-result invariant and its cursor-based eligibility rule, rather than a demand to retain all historical data or to add a production memory service.
findings.requested_revision: Define a conservative dependency/retention rule for already delivered results: keep any still-required original mandatory, or refuse before a later call if it is unavailable. Keeping all tool results mandatory until the execution ends is one bounded option. State how the runtime decides eligibility and cover the A-then-B follow-up case; do not treat receipt by an earlier stateless call as evidence that the original can safely disappear.
findings.validation_limit: Constructive static trace of the PROPOSED rules only; no runtime or model executed.

findings.title: The admitted JSON domain needs an explicit representation at the JSONB storage boundary

candidate_anchors.relevance: Plans existing stores without SQL migration and declares limits supporting escaped control-character strings.
Admits strings without lone surrogates, including U+0000, and requires preservation of value and canonical bytes.
Requires one V2 codec for stores and validation.
Promises shared canonical validation across memory and PostgreSQL but does not specify a reversible storage encoding.

current_source_anchors.relevance: The existing writer stores checkpoint.state directly as $9::jsonb.

findings.concrete_counterexample: A successful synthetic echo returns a string of 4096 U+0000 characters. It has no lone surrogate, is one JSON node, and its canonical JSON is 24578 UTF-8 bytes, below 32768. An illustrative user frame containing it is 24989 UTF-16 units, below 32000. PostgreSQL jsonb rejects decoded U+0000 in strings or object keys even when the JSON text spells it as \u0000. Keeping the current direct state-to-jsonb representation therefore makes this admitted COMPLETE output deterministically unpersistable; ordinary canonical escaping alone cannot fix it.
findings.material_impact: The generic save-failure stop protects settlement, so this finding does not allege duplicate effects or fabricated success. The gap is the unstated HOW connecting the declared complete JSON domain to the required real PostgreSQL checkpoint path. A future persistence test is not a substitute for that representation decision.
findings.requested_revision: Specify a reversible, byte-preserving V2 storage codec for values or keys that JSONB cannot represent directly, including decode and digest validation, or explicitly constrain the admitted domain and define the resulting availability classification. Preserve the original broader program requirements as open if the first slice is narrowed. Add the U+0000 value/key case to the future memory/PostgreSQL boundary criteria.
findings.validation_limit: The byte counts and JSON round trip were checked with Python stdlib. The PostgreSQL JSONB restriction is a manual technical inference from the direct ::jsonb boundary and known JSONB semantics, not an executed database test or an independently fetched reference; no PostgreSQL or network was invoked.

next_largest_gap.description: Separate delivery acknowledgement from the lifetime of evidence still needed by subsequent stateless decisions; make the dependency/refusal rule explicit before T3 submission.
